newsitem.title: UK: British factory gate prices flat in August.
newsitem.headline: British factory gate prices flat in August.

text.p: Prices of goods at British factory gates were flat in August, while raw material costs edged up modestly despite a steep rise in oil prices, the Office for National Statistics (ONS) said on Monday.

Unadjusted output prices were flat during the month, producing a 2.0 percent rise on the same month last year. This was in line with most market forecasts and was the lowest rate of increase since July 1994.
At the same time, seasonally adjusted input prices edged up by 0.3 percent, producing a 2.2 percent year-on-year increase.

The ONS said a sharp 3.5 percent monthly rise in the oil price component of the index -- which produced a dramatic 28.4 percent yearly surge -- was more than offset by falls in prices of rubber, paper and seasonal food.
Analysts said the figures boosted the government's chances of hitting its stringent 2.5 percent target for underlying inflation by the time its term in office ends early in 1997.
But others cautioned that a pickup in demand was starting to feed through into higher consumer prices, which may be more evident when the retail price index for August is released on Thursday.
